findings.title: listRecentAuditEvents 'actor' filter still queries subject column — schema migration deferred again (D70 SO-001 / D68 pre-scoped #5)
findings.description: D70 SO-001 closed by D70 T3 SO-7 PARTIAL only: AuditFatigueReaderOptions.actor (audit-reader.ts:14) added but the underlying SQL mapping is unchanged. runtime-store.ts:625-627 still maps `actor` filter to `eq(auditEvents.subject, actor)`. Subject for owner replay events = 'owner' (sentinel); subject for fatigue decisions = tool name; subject for subagent audits = ownerSubject (the actual human). Cross-actor replay rejection will silently match against ANY of these tokens, not the actor. D71 pre-scoped #1 first-class — must add migration 0014 (actor text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'), update schema.ts, appendAuditEvent contract (~20 emit sites to thread actor), then runtime-store.ts:626 swaps to eq(auditEvents.actor, actor).

audit-service.ts:25: `subject: entry.ownerSubject ?? entry.role`
schema.ts:173-194 auditEvents table has NO actor column (only audit_id/run_id/conversation_id/action/subject/detail/created_at/correlation_id per migration 0013)

Update schema.ts (auditEvents table) + appendAuditEvent contract (add `actor` field) + ALL emit sites to populate actor (wechatIn-user, telegram-update, schedule-worker, owner-handle, fatigue.decision at wechat-inbound-butler.ts:583). findings.title: owner-routes/memories.ts handleBatch line 325 returns raw `err.message` in per-id failure list (PG driver error leaks to owner)

findings.title: channel-outbound.ts:59 returns 'telegram API non-JSON: <raw>' to channel reply path — operator vocabulary leaks to wechat
findings.description: channel-outbound.ts:59 returns `telegram API non-JSON: ${raw.slice(0, 200)}` to the wechat reply (this propagates to the bot's reply to the user when telegram delivery fails). Owner sees raw telegram API response fragment. Same pattern at line 71 `telegram API HTTP ${res.status}` (English operator vocabulary) and line 77 `telegram API timeout after ${timeoutMs}ms`. These reach the channel-outbound callers (channel-inbound.ts handles telegram webhook delivery), which then propagates to the bot's failure message. Owner sees 'telegram API non-JSON: {"ok":false,"error_code":401,"description":"Unauthorized"}' instead of a Chinese owner-friendly message.

channel-outbound.ts:68-72: `if (!res.ok || !ok) { return { ok: false, reason: description ?? \`telegram API HTTP ${res.status}\` } }`

D62 T1 owner-jargon protocol applies to user-visible bot replies (chat surface), not just HTTP API
findings.fix_hint: Map channel error reasons to Chinese owner-jargon in channel-outbound.ts OR at the channel-inbound.ts boundary that translates to bot reply. Add `mapChannelErrorToOwnerJargon(reason: string)` helper. Pattern: 'telegram API non-JSON' → 'Telegram 暂时无法响应，请稍后重试'; 'telegram API HTTP 4xx' → 'Telegram 配置无效，请检查 Bot Token'; 'telegram API timeout' → 'Telegram 响应超时，请稍后重试'.

findings.title: safe-owner-error.ts is dead-weight in pre-commit harness: console.error can crash on missing stderr (unlikely but worth noting)
findings.description: safe-owner-error.ts:35 uses `console.error(...)` which writes to process.stderr. If stderr is closed (rare in production but possible in tests with mock stdio), the write throws EPIPE and propagates back through the catch chain — but the helper already caught the original error, so a secondary EPIPE would surface as an uncaught exception in the request handler. In the harness, vitest captures stderr so this doesn't happen. Per D63 T1 F-11 protocol, defensive wrap inside safeOwnerError itself (try { console.error } catch {}) is overkill — but worth noting.
findings.evidence:
safe-owner-error.ts:35-39: `console.error('[safe-owner-error]', { ...errInfo, context: context ?? null, fallback })`
harness.ts:194: vitest captures stderr via default vi.spyOn
Production: real stderr, no risk
D63 T1 F-11: did not add inner try/catch in safe-owner-error
findings.fix_hint: No fix. Confirm defensive wrap is unnecessary in practice. Document in safe-owner-error.ts JSDoc: 'requires writable stderr (true for all production + harness targets)'. Move to dont-fix category in batch commit.
